quote: Theorem 4.1 Let Xλ1, Xλ2, . . . , Xλn be independent random variables with Xλi ∼ W(α, λi), where λi > 0, i = 1, . . . , n, and let Xθ1, Xθ2, . . . , Xθn be another set of independent random variables with Xθi ∼ W(α, θi), where θi > 0, i = 1, . . . , n. Then for 0 < α ≤ 1, (λ1, . . . , λn) ≼w (θ1, . . . , θn) ⇒ Xn:n^λ ≤rh Xn:n^θ.
family: independent Weibull W(α, λi) with common shape 0 < α ≤ 1
compared: two parallel systems under weak supermajorization of scale vectors

quote: Corollary 4.2 Let Xλ1, Xλ2, . . . , Xλn be independent random variables with Xλi ∼ W(α, λi), where λi > 0, i = 1, . . . , n, and let Xθ1, Xθ2, . . . , Xθn be another set of independent random variables with Xθi ∼ W(α, θi), where θi > 0, i = 1, . . . , n. Then for 0 < α ≤ 1, (λ1, . . . , λn) ≼m (θ1, . . . , θn) ⇒ Xn:n^λ ≤rh Xn:n^θ.
compared: parallel systems under majorization of scales
ambiguity: Also proved by Khaledi et al. (2011) for generalized gamma with p = q < 1.

quote: Theorem 4.3 Let Xλ1, Xλ2 be independent random variables with Xλi ∼ W(α, λi) where λi > 0, i = 1, 2, and let Xθ1, Xθ2 be independent random variables with Xθi ∼ W(α, θi) where θi > 0, i = 1, 2. Then (λ1, λ2) ≼m (θ1, θ2) ⇒ r2:2^θ(t)/r2:2^λ(t) is increasing in t, for 0 < α ≤ 1.
compared: ratio of reverse hazard rates of the two maxima under majorization

quote: Theorem 4.4 Let Xλ1, Xλ2 be independent random variables with Xλi ∼ W(α, λi) where λi > 0, i = 1, 2, and let Xθ1, Xθ2 be independent random variables with Xθi ∼ W(α, θi) where θi > 0, i = 1, 2. Then for 0 < α ≤ 1, (λ1, λ2) ≼m (θ1, θ2) ⇒ X2:2^λ ≤lr X2:2^θ.
ambiguity: Generalizes Dykstra et al. (1997) Theorem 3.1 from exponential to Weibull; open for n > 2 with full majorization.

quote: Example 4.5 Let (Xλ1, Xλ2) be a vector of heterogeneous Weibull random variables, W(α, λi), with α = 2 and scale parameter vector (1.5, 2). Let (Xθ1, Xθ2) be a vector of heterogeneous Weibull random variables, W(α, θi), with α = 2 and scale parameter vector (1, 2.5). Obviously (λ1, λ2) ≼m (θ1, θ2), however X2:2^λ ≰lr X2:2^θ since f2:2^θ(t)/f2:2^λ(t) is not increasing in t as it can be seen from Figure 1.
compared: majorized scale vectors do not yield lr ordering when α > 1

conclusion.direction: X2:2^λ not <=lr X2:2^θ — density ratio not increasing

quote: Theorem 4.6 Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent random variables following the multiple-outlier Weibull model such that Xi ∼ W(α, λ1) for i = 1, . . . , p and Xj ∼ W(α, λ2) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1, λ2 > 0. Let Y1, . . . , Yn be another set ... such that Yi ∼ W(α, θ1) for i = 1, . . . , p and Yj ∼ W(α, θ2) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with θ1, θ2 > 0. Then for 0 < α ≤ 1, (λ1,...,λ1,λ2,...,λ2) ≼m (θ1,...,θ1,θ2,...,θ2) ⇒ rn:n^θ(t)/rn:n^λ(t) is increasing in t, where p + q = n.
model: parallel system, multiple-outlier model (p + q = n)
compared: ratio of reverse hazard rates under majorization of the two-level scale vectors

quote: Theorem 4.7 Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent random variables following the multiple-outlier Weibull model such that Xi ∼ W(α, λ1) for i = 1, . . . , p and Xj ∼ W(α, λ2) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1, λ2 > 0. Let Y1, . . . , Yn be another set ... with Yi ∼ W(α, θ1), Yj ∼ W(α, θ2), θ1, θ2 > 0. Then for 0 < α ≤ 1, (λ1·p, λ2·q) ≼m (θ1·p, θ2·q) ⇒ Xn:n^λ ≤lr Xn:n^θ.

conclusion.direction: Xn:n^λ <=lr Xn:n^θ (more dispersed scales give lr-larger maximum)

quote: Theorem 4.8 Let Xλ1, Xλ be independent random variables with Xλ1 ∼ W(α, λ1) and Xλ ∼ W(α, λ) where λ1, λ > 0. Let Yλ1*, Yλ be independent random variables with Yλ1* ∼ W(α, λ1*) and Yλ ∼ W(α, λ), where λ1*, λ > 0. Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then for any α > 0, (λ1, λ) ≼w (λ1*, λ) ⇒ r2:2*(t)/r2:2(t) is increasing in t.
model: parallel system (n = 2, common component scale λ)
compared: ratio of reverse hazard rates under weak majorization

quote: Theorem 4.9 Let Xλ1, Xλ ... Yλ1*, Yλ ... Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then for any α > 0, (λ1, λ) ≼w (λ1*, λ) ⇒ X2:2 ≤lr Y2:2.
compared: two parallel systems under weak majorization with λ1* smallest

hypotheses.text: λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*) and (λ1, λ) ≼w (λ1*, λ)

quote: Example 4.10 Let (Xλ1, Xλ) be a vector of heterogeneous Weibull random variables with α = 0.3 and scale parameters λ = 0.2 and λ1 = 3.5. Let (Yλ1*, Yλ) be a vector of heterogeneous Weibull random variables with α = 0.3 and scale parameters λ = 0.2 and λ1* = 2. Obviously (λ1, λ) ≼w (λ1*, λ) and λ ≤ λ1* ≤ λ1. However X2:2 ≰lr Y2:2 since f2:2*(t)/f2:2(t) is not increasing in t as it can be seen from Figure 2. Analogously, from Figure 3, it can be seen that X2:2 ≰lr Y2:2 when α = 1.3.
compared: weak majorization holds but λ1* not smallest — lr fails

conclusion.direction: X2:2 not <=lr Y2:2 for both α = 0.3 and α = 1.3

quote: Theorem 4.11 Let Xλ1, Xλ2 be independent random variables with Xλi ∼ W(α, λi) where λi > 0, i = 1, 2, and let Xθ1, Xθ2 be another set of independent random variables with Xθi ∼ W(α, θi) where θi > 0, i = 1, 2. Suppose θ1 ≤ λ1 ≤ λ2 ≤ θ2. Then (λ1, λ2) ≼w (θ1, θ2) implies that X2:2^λ ≤lr X2:2^θ, for 0 < α ≤ 1.
compared: two parallel systems under interlaced, weakly majorized scales

hypotheses.text: θ1 ≤ λ1 ≤ λ2 ≤ θ2 and (λ1, λ2) ≼w (θ1, θ2)

quote: Theorem 4.12 Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent random variables following the multiple-outlier Weibull model such that Xi ∼ W(α, λ1) for i = 1, . . . , p and Xj ∼ W(α, λ) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1, λ > 0. Let Y1, . . . , Yn be another set ... with Yi ∼ W(α, λ1*), Yj ∼ W(α, λ), λ1*, λ > 0. Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then for any α > 0, (λ1·p, λ·q) ≼w (λ1*·p, λ·q) ⇒ rn:n*(t)/rn:n(t) is increasing in t.
model: parallel system, multiple-outlier model (p + q = n)
compared: ratio of reverse hazard rates of multiple-outlier maxima

quote: Theorem 4.13 Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent random variables such that Xi ∼ W(α, λ1) for i = 1, . . . , p and Xj ∼ W(α, λ) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1, λ > 0. Let Y1, . . . , Yn be independent nonnegative random variables with Yi ∼ W(α, λ1*) for i = 1, . . . , p and Yj ∼ W(α, λ) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1*, λ > 0. Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then (λ1·p, λ·q) ≼w (λ1*·p, λ·q) ⇒ Xn:n ≤lr Yn:n, for p + q = n and any α > 0.
compared: two multiple-outlier systems under weak majorization

hypotheses.text: λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*) and (λ1·p, λ·q) ≼w (λ1*·p, λ·q)

ambiguity: Analogous to Theorem 4.7 without the α ≤ 1 restriction but with the extra min constraint.
